item.title: Tampa Bay Rays leaders begin making sales pitch for new stadium project
item.description: The Tampa Bay Rays and the team’s new CEO are taking their sales pitch on the road.The team, which has been widely reported, looks to build a new stadium in Tampa and has identified the Dale Mabry campus of Hillsborough College as the right spot. item.title: Tampa picks developer for workforce housing, commercial project
item.description: A major redevelopment that will bring a mixed-use project with affordable housing and commercial space to a section of downtown Tampa is one step closer to reality.Tampa city officials have selected a developer for the redevelopment of four city-owned properties north of downtown. item.title: Hillsborough County delivers $24M to USF mixed-use project
item.description: The University of South Florida has scored another $24 million to transform its defunct The Claw golf course into a mixed-use development called the Fletcher District. The Hillsborough County Commission voted unanimously during its March 4 meeting to give USF $24 million for infrastructure and public safety improvements for the new district that will help connect it to the nearby, on-campus football stadium. item.title: Ringling College sells Englewood Art Center
item.description: Following nearly 20 years of ownership, Ringling College has sold the Englewood Art Center in south Sarasota County. The new owner is the Hermitage Artist Retreat, which purchased the property at 350 S. McCall Road at the end of November 2025 for $100, according to Sarasota County property records. The two entities announced the transfer of ownership in a joint statement March 9.On 2 acres, the Englewood Art Center includes two buildings that total 10,000 square feet.
